legal.title: Advanced electronic signature under the eIDAS Regulation
legal.body: Regulation (EU) 910/2014 (eIDAS) gives legal effect to electronic signatures and defines the advanced electronic signature in its Article 26. This is how DocuFirma meets it:

unique.title: Uniquely linked to the signer
unique.body: Each signer receives a unique, personal link by email and signs with their own stroke.

identify.title: Capable of identifying them
identify.body: We record name, email, IP address, device and the biometric data of the signature.

control.title: Under their sole control
control.body: The signer creates the signature by hand, on their own device, after reading the document.

integrity.title: Detects any change
integrity.body: The SHA-256 fingerprint and the qualified timestamp (Art. 42) reveal any subsequent modification.

legal.disclaimer: DocuFirma provides advanced electronic signatures, not qualified electronic signatures.

q1.q: Is a DocuFirma signature legally valid?
q1.a: Yes. It is an advanced electronic signature under Article 26 of the eIDAS Regulation, admissible as evidence in legal proceedings across the EU. For the few acts that legally require a qualified signature or a notarial deed, it does not replace those requirements.

q2.a: It is proof, issued by a qualified trust service provider, that a document existed with specific content at an exact date and time. Under Article 41 of eIDAS, the accuracy of that date and the integrity of the data are presumed.

q3.q: Does the signer need an account or to install anything?
q3.a: No. They receive an email with a unique link, review the document in their browser and sign with a finger, a stylus or the mouse. It works on phones, tablets and computers.

q4.q: Which biometric data is captured and how is it protected?
q4.a: We capture the signature stroke (coordinates, pressure, tilt and timing) with the signer's explicit consent. It is encrypted with AES-256, used only as evidence of the signature and kept for the period stated in the privacy policy.

q5.q: What happens if I don't use all my monthly signatures?
q5.a: Signatures included in the plan renew every billing cycle and do not roll over. Pack signatures never expire and are only used once your monthly signatures run out.

q6.a: One signature is one signer completing an envelope, even if they sign several documents at once. An envelope with three signers uses three signatures. If someone declines or the envelope expires, the pending signatures go back to your balance.

q7.q: Can I verify a signed document?
q7.a: Yes. On the verification page you can enter the DF-XXXX-XXXX code printed on the document or upload the PDF: we compute its fingerprint in your browser and check it against the sealed original, without the file ever leaving your device.

q8.a: Yes. You can cancel your subscription from your dashboard at any time. You keep access to your history and your signed documents.

senderSteps.s1: Create your account and upload one or more PDFs, images or Word documents.

privacy.description: How we process the personal data of users and signers.

s1.p: [COMPANY NAME], tax ID [TAX ID], [ADDRESS]. Data protection officer: [DPO EMAIL].

s2.p: We process your account data (name, email, company, optional tax ID), billing and usage data to provide the service (Art. 6.1.b GDPR), comply with legal obligations (Art. 6.1.c) and improve the service (legitimate interest, Art. 6.1.f).

s3.p: For documents sent by our users, DocuFirma acts as a data processor. We process name, email, IP address, device data, approximate location and signing events to produce the signature evidence.

s4.p: The signature stroke (coordinates, pressure, tilt and timing) may be biometric data (Art. 9 GDPR). It is only captured with the signer's explicit consent, encrypted with AES-256-GCM, used exclusively as evidence of the signature and kept for [5] years after signing, unless legal proceedings require longer retention.

s5.p: We use providers located in, or with servers in, the EU: Supabase (database and storage, Frankfurt), Vercel (hosting, Frankfurt), Stripe (payments), Resend (email), Mensatek (timestamping) and Sentry (error monitoring). Any international transfer relies on standard contractual clauses.

s6.p: Account data is kept while the account is active. Completed envelopes and their evidence are kept for [5] years to defend potential claims. Invoices are kept for the periods required by tax law.

s7.p: You can exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction and portability by writing to [PRIVACY EMAIL] or by deleting your account in Settings. You may also lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es).

s1.p: We only use strictly necessary cookies: the user session (sb-*), the language preference (NEXT_LOCALE) and security cookies from our payment provider during checkout. They do not require consent (Art. 22.2 LSSI-CE).

s2.p: DocuFirma does not use third-party analytics or advertising cookies. If they are added in the future, we will ask for your prior consent through a banner.

s3.p: You can delete or block cookies in your browser settings. If you block technical cookies you will not be able to log in.

signature-policy.description: How a signature is created, preserved and verified in DocuFirma.

s1.p: Biometric advanced electronic signature under Article 26 of Regulation (EU) 910/2014 (eIDAS), complemented by a qualified timestamp under its Articles 41 and 42.

s2.p: The signer receives by email a unique link with 256 bits of entropy. Only the SHA-256 hash of the link is stored. Name, email, IP address, user agent, device, approximate location and the event timeline are recorded.

s3.p: After reviewing the whole document and accepting the consent (a versioned, recorded text), the signer draws their signature. For every point we capture coordinates, pressure, tilt, pointer type and a high-resolution timestamp.

s4.p: We compute the SHA-256 fingerprint of every original document, of the biometric file and of the final signed PDF. An RFC 3161 timestamp is requested from Mensatek (policy OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.5734.3.18.1) over the latter and over the evidence certificate.

s5.p: Anyone can verify a document at docufirma.es/verify with its code or fingerprint. The timestamp can be checked independently with OpenSSL (openssl ts -verify).

s6.p: Evidence is kept encrypted for [5] years. Access is restricted to server processes and, upon request, to judicial authorities.
